docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PulseGuard is a Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) platform developed as part of a fourth-year DevOps project.

The platform monitors knee replacement patients during the first six weeks of home recovery, flags patients who drift from their expected trajectory, and presents the information through a GP dashboard.

The project currently consists of:

  • Patient registry service
  • Telemetry ingestion service
  • Alert and flag evaluation service
  • React frontend dashboard
  • Recovery simulator

docs.title: Project Goals
docs.text:
The primary goals of PulseGuard are:

  • Monitor knee replacement recovery remotely
  • Detect patients drifting from expected recovery trajectories
  • Support GP decision-making with ranked, explained flags
  • Demonstrate modern DevOps practices
  • Showcase containerisation, CI/CD and cloud deployment strategies

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PulseGuard exposes three backend services, each on its own port.

Service Base URL Patient service http://localhost:8001 Telemetry service http://localhost:8002 Alert service http://localhost:8003

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text:
Returns the health status of the service.

Response:

{ "status": "ok" }

docs.title: GET /patients
docs.text:
Returns all registered patients.

Response:

[
  {
    "id": 1,
    "name": "John Doe",
    "age": 67,
    "surgery_date": "2026-10-07",
    "walking_ability": "unaided"
  }
]

Walking ability values: unaided, stick, frame.

docs.title: GET /patients/{id}
docs.text:
Returns a single patient by ID.

Returns 404 if the patient does not exist.

docs.title: POST /patients
docs.text:
Creates a new patient.

Request body:

{
  "name": "string",
  "age": 18,
  "surgery_date": "YYYY-MM-DD",
  "walking_ability": "unaided"
}

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: Returns the health status of the service.

docs.title: POST /readings
docs.text:
Stores a daily reading for a patient.

One reading per patient per day. A second POST for the same patient and day replaces the first.

Returns 201 on success.

Request body:

{
  "patient_id": 1,
  "day": 7,
  "steps": 2400,
  "resting_hr": 72,
  "sleep_hours": 7.2,
  "pain": 3
}

docs.title: GET /readings/{patient_id}
docs.text:
Returns all readings for a patient, ordered by day.

Returns [] if no readings exist.

docs.title: DELETE /readings
docs.text:
Deletes all readings for all patients.

Returns 204.

docs.title: GET /simulation
docs.text:
Returns the current simulator configuration.

Response:

{
  "seconds_per_day": 1.5,
  "total_days": 42
}

docs.title: PUT /simulation
docs.text:
Updates the simulator configuration.

Request body:

{
  "seconds_per_day": 1.5,
  "total_days": 42
}

docs.title: GET /health
docs.text: Returns the health status of the service.

docs.title: GET /status
docs.text:
Returns the health status of all three services and the current simulator configuration.

Response:

{
  "services": {
    "alert": "ok",
    "patient": "ok",
    "telemetry": "ok"
  },
  "simulation": {
    "seconds_per_day": 1.5,
    "total_days": 42
  }
}

docs.title: GET /patients
docs.text:
Returns all patients ranked by flag count, then by recovery day.

Each patient includes:

  • Current recovery day and week
  • Latest reading
  • Heart rate baseline
  • Three flag evaluations (mobilisation, complication, pain)
  • Total flag count

Flag status values: clear, flagged, pending.

docs.title: GET /patients/{id}
docs.text:
Returns full detail for a single patient.

Includes all fields from GET /patients plus:

  • Full reading history
  • Expected step band per week

Returns 404 if the patient does not exist.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
PulseGuard is a microservices-based Remote Patient Monitoring platform for knee replacement recovery.

The system ingests daily patient readings, evaluates them against recovery rules, and presents the results through a GP dashboard.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text:
graph TD
    SIM[Simulator] --> TEL[Telemetry Service :8002]
    SIM --> PAT[Patient Service :8001]
    PAT --> ALT[Alert Service :8003]
    TEL --> ALT
    ALT --> DASH[Dashboard :3000]

All five components run as containers under Docker Compose.

docs.title: Patient Service
docs.text:
Maintains the patient registry.

Responsibilities:

  • Store patient records (name, age, surgery date, walking ability)
  • Expose patient list and individual patient lookup
  • Walking ability is used by the alert service to adjust step targets

Port: 8001

docs.title: Telemetry Service
docs.text:
Stores daily readings. Has no knowledge of clinical meaning.

Responsibilities:

  • Accept and store one reading per patient per day
  • Expose readings by patient in day order
  • Manage simulator configuration (seconds per day, total days)

A reading contains:

  • Steps
  • Resting heart rate
  • Sleep hours
  • Pain score (0–10)
  • Recovery day

Port: 8002

docs.title: Alert Service
docs.text:
Evaluates readings against recovery rules. Stores nothing.

Responsibilities:

  • Fetch patients and readings from the other services on each request
  • Compute the expected step band for each recovery week
  • Calculate each patient's heart rate baseline (mean of first three days)
  • Evaluate three flags per patient
  • Return patients ranked by flag count

Port: 8003

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
React frontend served by Nginx.

Responsibilities:

  • Display patients ranked by urgency
  • Show flag status and reason per patient
  • Render trend charts against the expected band and personal baseline
  • Display demo clock when simulator is attached

Port: 3000

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
Replays synthetic six-week recoveries for five patients.

Responsibilities:

  • POST one reading per patient per day on each tick
  • Drift two patients on purpose so all three flags fire
  • Run as a container; does not expose an HTTP port

docs.title: Mobilisation
docs.text:
Steps below the expected weekly band for seven consecutive days, or no week-on-week increase after day 14.

The step target is adjusted by walking ability: unaided 1.0, stick 0.85, frame 0.70.

Status: pending until day 7.

docs.title: Complication
docs.text:
Resting heart rate 10 BPM or more above the personal baseline for three consecutive days.

Baseline is the mean resting heart rate from the first three days of readings.

Status: pending until day 3.

docs.title: Pain
docs.text:
Pain score 7 or above for three consecutive days, or sleep under five hours with pain 5 or above for three consecutive nights.

Status: pending until day 3.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text: All notable changes to the PulseGuard project are documented in this file.

docs.title: Microservices and Docker Compose
docs.text:
Split the backend into three independent services:

  • Patient service (registry, port 8001)
  • Telemetry service (ingestion and storage, port 8002)
  • Alert service (flag evaluation, port 8003)

Each service has its own Dockerfile and health check.

Docker Compose wires the full stack with startup ordering via health checks. One command starts all five containers.

docs.title: Alert and Flag System
docs.text:
Implemented three clinical flag rules:

  • Mobilisation: steps below expected band or no weekly gain after day 14
  • Complication: resting heart rate 10+ above personal baseline for three consecutive days
  • Pain: pain score 7+ for three days, or short sleep with elevated pain for three nights

Expected step band defined per recovery week, adjusted by walking ability.

Heart rate baseline computed from the first three days of readings.

docs.title: Recovery Simulator
docs.text:
Replaced random telemetry with realistic six-week recovery curves for five patients.

Two patients drift on purpose:

  • Mark Ryan: heart rate rising from day 18 (complication flag)
  • Sarah Smith: elevated pain and poor sleep around days 24–28 (pain flag)
  • Tom Murphy: step plateau from day 15 (mobilisation flag)

docs.title: GP Dashboard
docs.text:
Rebuilt around flags:

  • Patients ranked by flag count
  • Flag status and reason displayed per patient
  • Trend charts: steps vs expected band, heart rate vs baseline, pain and sleep
  • Demo clock labelled on screen

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
Added 33 automated tests across the three services:

  • Patient service: 6 tests
  • Telemetry service: 6 tests
  • Alert service: 21 tests (flag logic and API)

docs.title: Initial Prototype
docs.text:
Implemented:

  • FastAPI backend
  • VitalReading data model
  • Telemetry ingestion endpoint
  • In-memory data storage
  • Synthetic patient telemetry generator
  • React dashboard
  • Risk classification engine
  • Statistics dashboard cards
  • Patient monitoring interface

docs.title: Alert Classification
docs.text:
Added support for:

  • NORMAL status
  • MODERATE RISK status
  • HIGH RISK status

Rules implemented:

  • Heart Rate > 110 BPM → HIGH RISK
  • Heart Rate > 95 BPM → MODERATE RISK
  • Sleep Hours < 5 → MODERATE RISK

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This runbook provides instructions for operating and troubleshooting the PulseGuard prototype.

docs.title: System Startup
docs.text:
Start the full stack:

docker compose up --build

Expected result: five containers start in order. The dashboard is available at http://localhost:3000.

docs.title: System Shutdown
docs.text: docker compose down

docs.title: Viewing Logs
docs.text:
All services:

docker compose logs -f

One service:

docker compose logs -f alert-service

Service names: patient-service, telemetry-service, alert-service, dashboard, simulator.

docs.title: Patient Service
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:8001/health.

Expected response:

{ "status": "ok" }

docs.title: Telemetry Service
docs.text: Open http://localhost:8002/health.

docs.title: Alert Service
docs.text: Open http://localhost:8003/health.

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
Open http://localhost:3000.

Expected result: patient cards and service status pills are visible.

docs.title: Dashboard Shows No Data
docs.text:
Possible cause: alert service not running.

Solution:

docker compose restart alert-service

docs.title: Service Shows as Down in Dashboard
docs.text:
Possible cause: container failed its health check.

Solution:

docker compose logs alert-service
docker compose restart alert-service

docs.title: Port Already in Use
docs.text:
Possible cause: another process is using one of the required ports (8001, 8002, 8003, 3000).

Solution: identify and stop the conflicting process, then restart the stack.

Windows:

netstat -ano | findstr :3000
taskkill /PID <pid> /F

docs.title: No Patient Data After Startup
docs.text:
Possible cause: simulator has not started yet or exited early.

Solution:

docker compose logs simulator
docker compose restart simulator

docs.title: Resetting All Data
docs.text:
Stop the stack, then start fresh:

docker compose down
docker compose up --build

All readings are stored in memory and are cleared on restart.

docs.title: Future Operational Features
docs.text:
Future versions of PulseGuard will include:

  • PostgreSQL with persistent storage
  • Structured logging with a request ID across services
  • Prometheus and Grafana dashboards
  • Alerting on service health
  • Kubernetes deployment

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide explains how to set up and run the PulseGuard prototype locally.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The following software must be installed:

  • Docker
  • Docker Compose
  • Git

docs.title: Clone Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Ibukunn7/pulseguard-prototype.git

Navigate into the repository:

cd pulseguard-prototype

docs.title: Running with Docker Compose
docs.text:
Build and start all services:

docker compose up --build

The following ports will be available:

Service Port Patient service 8001 Telemetry service 8002 Alert service 8003 Dashboard 3000

The simulator starts automatically and begins replaying patient data.

Open the dashboard at http://localhost:3000.

docs.title: Stopping the Stack
docs.text: docker compose down

docs.title: Running Without Docker
docs.text: If Docker is not available, each service can be run manually.

docs.title: Manual Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.12
  • Node.js 20
  • npm

docs.title: Patient Service
docs.text:
cd services/patient-service
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --port 8001

docs.title: Telemetry Service
docs.text:
cd services/telemetry-service
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --port 8002

docs.title: Alert Service
docs.text:
cd services/alert-service
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn main:app --port 8003

docs.title: Dashboard
docs.text:
cd frontend
npm install
npm run dev

The dashboard will be available at http://localhost:5173.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text:
cd simulator
pip install -r requirements.txt
python patient_simulator.py

docs.title: Expected Behaviour
docs.text:
The simulator generates five patient recoveries over 42 days.

The alert service evaluates readings and flags patients who drift.

The dashboard displays patients ranked by flag count and updates every two seconds during the demo.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
PulseGuard Testing Documentation

Overview Testing was performed throughout development to verify that telemetry data could successfully travel through the system and be displayed on the dashboard.

Testing Strategy The current prototype uses manual testing to validate functionality.

Testing focuses on:

Telemetry generation API communication Alert classification Dashboard updates

Test Case 1 - Backend Health Check Objective Verify that the FastAPI backend starts correctly.

Steps Start the backend service. Navigate to: http://127.0.0.1:8000 Expected Result { "message": "PulseGuard Backend Running" } Result PASS

Test Case 2 - Telemetry Ingestion Objective Verify that the backend receives telemetry readings.

Steps Start the simulator. Monitor backend logs. Expected Result Successful POST requests appear in backend logs.

Result PASS

Test Case 3 - Alert Classification Objective Verify that alert rules classify patient risk correctly.

Rules Tested High Risk Heart Rate > 110 BPM Expected:

HIGH RISK Moderate Risk Heart Rate > 95 BPM Expected:

MODERATE RISK Moderate Risk Sleep Hours < 5 Expected:

MODERATE RISK Result PASS

Test Case 4 - Dashboard Updates Objective Verify that the React dashboard displays incoming telemetry.

Steps Start backend. Start simulator. Start frontend. Expected Result Patient information appears and updates automatically.

Result PASS

Test Case 5 - Dashboard Statistics Objective Verify that summary cards display accurate patient counts.

Statistics Tested Total Patients Normal Patients Moderate Risk Patients High Risk Patients Result PASS
